A Common Enemy

The Autonomous Bastards Collective, a proud proponent of piracy and lawlessness across the galaxy (and this, for decades), is once again drawing the attention of your intelligence services. There are rumors of the pirates not merely banding together, but also equipping themselves with recently discovered weapons from an Endless ruin. Though it is hard to know how much of this is fact and how much is baseless chatter, it couldn't hurt to send both private and public signals indicating the galaxy stands firm against these outlaws.
In the next $Timer [turn] Gain a new Ally.
FEDERATE
Make a public show of unity against the ABC. Your intelligence services will send their own very clear messages in private…
Alliances are set up in the Diplomacy screen, and require Influence to obtain.
It seems that the civilized forces of the galaxy have once again sent the ABC running for cover. Sadly they're a lot like cockraoches; once you have an infestation, you know they'll be back again.
It looks like any future transgressions of the ABC will have to be faced alone. Hopefully, they'll fall back to their usual habits of backstabbing and internecine disputes.
Thieves And Traitors

It seems that certain rebellious elements within the Academy have decided to formally oppose Isyander's vision of the future. It is said that they refuse to accept some of the potential risks of his crusade, which happen to include the possible eradication of intelligent life. Breaking into the open, these rogue fleets of dissenting heroes are out in the galaxy, attempting to foment rebellion and interrupt the long-view strategic game that Isyander is playing. No longer being entirely sure of his own so-called followers, the leader of the Academy requests your help in bringing them down.
Hunt down and defeat the three rebel fleets.
GIVE CHASE
Put an end to the rogue heroes that are opposing Isyander's grand plan.
The location of the fleets are indicated with a quest marker.
Not an easy task, dealing with contentious Heroes. Should you choose to ultimately side with Isyander, you will have a powerful ally. And if not, you have at least allayed his suspicions…
You have failed the quest!
Betrayors
Academy [ship] ship where a betrayer was defeated
Academy Gift
Incoming!

So they're at it again, are they? Reconaissance data indicates that a group of pirates have targeted one of your systems. Allowing that to happen on your watch will certainly cause some annoyances in the next election. Would you really let a bunch of criminals upset your carefully constructed vision for your empire?
The pirates must be taught a lethal lesson, either by the use of your fleets or by the clear indication that they are set up to fail. As always, it is your political acumen -- or budgetary needs -- that will determine how best to handle this.
Destroy the fleet or assign a Guardian-class Hero.
DEFEND
Remove the pirate threat from the $YourSiegedSystemName system, either by destroying it directly or by assigning a Guardian-class Hero to plan its defense. They will arrive in $Timer [turn] turns.
Hero class types can be found on the Hero Overview Screen. You have two ways to win: assigning an hero or defeating the pirates.
Whether this was the ABC probing for weaknesses or a separate group, it's good to send a message that says, "This is a very bad idea."
Well, that didn't go as you had hoped. I wonder what unpleasant nicknames they'll invent for you in social media?
The Collective
Forged in Battle

A Hero comes to you with an unusual request. They would like to have a formal dispensation -- an order from you -- to be allowed to hunt down other Heroes in the galaxy. This seems a bit odd, of course. An old tradition? A hazing ritual? A practical joke gone too far? However, when a Hero wins a battle they gain power from which you benefit, and in addition to this, the notoriety and image of your empire will certainly gain stature. Very well, then... Let the Heroes play their games, as long as you can profit from it. Let the hunt begin!
Hunt and injure $ShipsCountName heros commanding ships within $Timer [turn] turns.
ENGAGE
It's time to let loose the dogs of war! Unleash your Hero on $ShipsCountName Fleets commanded by Heroes within $DurationName Turns.
Tip: These enemy Fleets will have a Hero Ship in their roster
While the idea of having Heroes hospitalizing each other as some sort of talent show is a bit disturbing, at least your Hero has gained valuable experience and appreciation for your open-mindedness.
Admittedly, it is not always the case that Hero Fleets are looking to be attacked. Hopefully your Hero has at least learned something, and not angered the Academy.
Opposing Hero
Opposing Fleet
Chapter 1: Strange Tidings

The only problem with dangerous secrets long left buried is that, eventually, some fool is bound to dig them up…
Archeologists and researchers from the Ursa Major Technopole have discovered evidence of an Endless-constructed superweapon. While it is not surprising that they created devastating armaments, the worry is that this one may either be active or at least able to be activated. There is no time to lose; get your explorers out there and figure out what is happening -- before the weapon ends up pointed at you.
Curiosities in several constellations need to be examined and their data compared to discover the origin of an Endless superweapon.
STUDY
The Curiosities to be examined will be show a quest indicator
Investigate the highlighted Curiosities in the galaxy.

The information that you have gathered shows that the effects of these weapons were formidable. They were capable of targeting elements as small as a ship and as large as a planet -- but occasionally seemed to fire into empty space. It doesn’t quite add up yet...
Sadly, there was not enough interest in your scientific community -- or not enough budget -- to complete the task. These mysteries shall remain mysterious…
Chapter 2: Weapon Without a Target

There are many elements of this Endless weapons system that need to be analyzed and understood -- from power sources to focusing technology to targeting systems. Any empire that wishes to get to the bottom of the mystery has one clear task: to become a lot smarter about the energies the Endless were able to harness and exploit.
It's time to rev up the research facilities and study the unknown.
In order to understand the elements of the Endless weapon system, increase the Science output of your faction, or sign a Science Treaty with another empire
LEARN
Increase SCI production to $Amount02 or sign a Science Treaty with another empire.
You can increase Science production with Improvements, Laws, Hero Skills, and Luxury Resources
Your scientists and engineers have learned a great deal, but are still scratching their heads; as usual, more knowledge leads to more questions. In this case, the question is: Why?
It seems that you were not quite fast enough in the pursuit of knowledge. The secrets of the Endless's weapon system will remain shrouded in mystery.
Chapter 3: Anomalous Data

When the Endless went big, they went very big. It appears that the weapon in question was not fired by any traditional means, but harnessed the gamma ray output of quasars and black holes to form a gamma ray of unthinkable intensity.
While the researchers first spent time amazed at what it was and what it could do, they soon came to wonder what exactly it did. They seem to have been used often, but little associated debris has been found. In fact, it seem that the weapons were firing into space with no obvious target.
Gather additional information, either on the use of the weapon or on its targets.
INVESTIGATE
Discover a new Endless-related Unique Planet, OR explore $Amount03 % of the galaxy .
Exploration Ships can be set to Auto-Explore to uncover hidden parts of the galaxy
Enough new information has come up to provide the plans for a module. Hopefully, with this module, the researchers can finally get some solid answers.
The galaxy is too vast, or your ships too slow. There is not enough information to continue the investigation, and this Endless mystery will stay unsolved.
Chapter 4: A Final Absolution

Out of all the sites that have been either visited or described in the discovered data, one appears to be the most promising. An Endless relic was close enough to the target to -- with luck -- have left some details of its use and its effects. In fact, it is possible that the relic played the role of an observer station during the weapon's use.
This, finally, may help explain exactly what the Endless were after in the empty voids of space... on the other hand, there is no way to know if the weapon is still active. Reinforcements would probably be a good idea; you never know who may show up with an interest in obtaining your knowledge.
See what remains at the location identified by your scientists.
IDENTIFY
Send a fleet to the location indicated by the quest flag.
Explore the indicated location
Defeat the Academy fleet!
To the victor goes the knowledge…

The survivors of the engagement fill you in on the details. The weapon was the most gruesome invention of the Endless, used to drain the life from the god-like creatures known as the Lost. When they were fired, thousands of years ago, the locations they targeted were not at all empty void, but living -- and now extinct -- beings.
Sadly, you were unable to determine what exactly went on at that location. Whatever it was, the Academy is passionately interested -- which indicates a strong likelihood that it concerned the Lost.

A Matter of Black and White

Economic development or environmental sustainability? An argument as old as sentient life has still not found its ultimate answer. Even now, differing voices within your government advocate strongly for one or the other approach.
Improve your industrial output at the risk of damage to the ecosystems, or promote conservation and responsible development at the risk of a decline in your economic power? As the supreme leader of your empire, the choice comes down to you.
Make the ecologists angry by enacting $IndustrialistLawsCountLocale industrialists laws.
Industrialist
Pass $IndustrialistLawsCountLocale Industrialist Laws.
Use the Senate Screen to select and pass Laws
Make the industrialists angry by enacting $EcologistLawsCountLocale ecologist Laws.
Ecologist
Pass $EcologistLawsCountLocale Ecologist Laws.
Use the Senate Screen to select and pass Laws
Done! Legislation moves ahead and the path of your empire shifts slightly. Forward, then, to a future where some day these two forces no longer pull in opposite directions.
Sometimes the choices are too difficult, and no choice is the ultimate outcome. But don't worry; even without you, they are able to continue bickering.

Wisdom Of The Past

Curious archaeologists speak to you of an ancient starfaring race called the Nakalim -- who may no longer be quite so ancient. History tells us that they hibernated en masse as their civilization collapsed, but little is known of their culture and history. Are you willing to redirect some exploration vessels to uncover some of the secrets of this unusual story? Perhaps you could even come to understand some of their unique and powerful technology.
Their civilization is an old one, so investigating Ruins type Curiosities is likely a good way to learn more.
DISCOVER
Investigate $NumberRuinsLocale ruins type curiosity.
These can be found anywhere, and more will appear as your level of Science increases.

Fascinating! Apparently they were worshippers of the Lost, and many of their technologies appeared as direct gifts from this incomprehensible species. Let us see exactly how the artifact you now own operates…

Unfortunately, there were not enough Curiosities (or not enough time) to determine the secrets behind the Nakalim. While much of the history of the galaxy is known to you, this part will remain hidden.
Nakalim [ship] ship where last Curiosity was discovered
Nakalim Reward Fleet
Death Without a Corpse

It is now accepted as proven fact that a race called the Lost -- giant, ethereal beings formed from primordial Dust -- used to live in the empty places between the stars and the constellations. Who knows what remains of them, now that records indicate that they were hunted to extinction? What vestiges of their glory or their death might you collect? Perhaps, if you send a vessel through those uncharted empty spaces, away from the starlanes, you may find some trace of what they left behind. If, that is, anything at all remains...
Travel between $NumberLocale solar systems without using the starlanes, and you may pick up traces of the Lost before they were hunted by the Endless.
TRAVERSE
Use the Warp Drive technology to travel $NumberLocale times without a starlane.
The Warp Drive technology is in the Science Quadrant of the Technology Tree.
Beautiful, but melancholy. Like all deaths, something great is lost and something precious is left behind. In the case of the Lost, all that is left behind is their Dust…
It seems that your efforts, like the Lost themselves, ran out of time. Perhaps some hidden things were meant to stay that way.
A Galaxy Far, Far Away

For some weeks now, sensors have been strangely occluded and scanning passes have been returning unexpected results. While this was chalked up to equipment or operator stress, solar winds, and choppy communications, the truth seems to be much stranger.
In fact, these sensor and scan anomalies should have been viewed as intruder alarm systems; it seems that unknown and invisible beings from another galaxy are beginning to circulate among us.
They may not be more scientifically advanced, but they certainly are different enough that our own science must leap forward to understand them.
Build $Number "Optics Research Labs" or "Stasis Singularity" Improvements.
ADVANCE
The technologies best suited to understanding these beings would be "Wave Function Control" Improvements or "Unified Tachyon Theory".
These technologies are found in the Science Quadrant of the Technology Tree. Some Improvements may not be available to every faction.

Unexpected and…delightful? Whatever these strange entities are, they are pleased to have made contact and insist that they come in peace. Or, at least, that if they do harm it is by accident. A small gift of their technology may give you a look into their strange world.
Alas, scientific advancement can be complicated and difficult. Whatever these strange beings may be, you will have to meet and understand them in some other way.
Umbral Choir [ship] ship where last Improvement was built
Umbral Choir Reward Fleet

Sbejru Mashmir

As the seventh pup of the seventh generation of seven-pup litters, Sbejru's origins are the mystical to the point where one suspects external interference. The early years of their life were little different from any other exotically apocryphal house pet, but that all changed after they stowed away on a Vaulter ship departing Auriga. Uplifted by a Dust event at the Lodestone of the Nine, Sbejru blossomed into a leader as capable as they are unusual. Though often looked down upon literally as well as figuratively, their efficient use of the war hammer usually prevents disobedience and snide comments from getting out of hand.
